t: Polo-like kinase (PLK) family | Enzymes | IUPHAR/BPS Guide to PHARMACOLOGY
s: The Polo-like kinases (PLK) are Ser/Thr kinases of the cell cycle that are involved in regulating mitotic entry, mitotic exit, spindle formation, cytokinesis, and meiosis [1,6]. PLK inhibitors are predicted to offer anti-proliferative potential for application in oncology [7,10].

t: Polo-like kinase - Wikipedia
s: September 7, 2025 - Plks are controlled at the level of protein synthesis and degradation, by the action of upstream kinases and phosphatases, and by localization to specific subcellular structures. Plks are activated by phosphorylation within a short region of the catalytic domain called the T-loop (or activation loop), with several serine/threonine phosphorylation sites in the loop identified.
